The test chip CESAME was developed in 0.18 µm CMOS technology with a die area of 11 mm².
The chip contains six identical logic cores, each with 240 base cells including D flip-flops, clock trees, and standard gates.
Three cores were studied: NORM (standard), ISO (isolated substrate), and RC (integrated decoupling capacitor).
The RC core includes a 1 nF integrated decoupling capacitor, increasing its area by 40% compared to the NORM core.
The ISO core uses a triple-well technique to isolate its substrate from the rest of the chip.
DPI immunity measurements were performed from 10 MHz to 1 GHz in 10 MHz steps.
The immunity criterion for DPI is a 20% ripple or 10% jitter in the output signal.
The immunity criterion for VF-TLP is a 0.4V output pulse.
At 50 MHz, the RC core requires 41 dBm of injected power to become susceptible, compared to 25 dBm for NORM and 34 dBm for ISO.
The RC core requires a 40V pulse to induce errors in VF-TLP, ISO requires 30V, and NORM requires 20V.
The peak magnetic field emission at 50 MHz is -47.5 dBm for NORM, -50.6 dBm for ISO, and -57.1 dBm for RC.
The RC core reduces emission by about 10 dBm compared to the NORM core.
The ISO core reduces emission by about 3 dBm compared to the NORM core.
The ranking of effectiveness is the same for both immunity and emission: RC > ISO > NORM.
The RC protection technique increases die area by 40% due to the integrated capacitor.
Substrate isolation (ISO core) limits substrate coupling and improves immunity and emission.
The triple-well technique in the ISO core reduces coupling capacitance between substrates.
The RC core's decoupling capacitor acts as a low-pass filter, attenuating high-frequency harmonics.
The study confirms that low-emission design rules also improve immunity.
The paper recommends integrated decoupling capacitors for best EMI reduction, but notes the cost and area trade-off.
Future work will explore near-field injection and new shielding methods for mixed-signal circuits.
